title: GOD model: Privacy Preserved AI School for Personal Assistant
extended_summary:
This paper proposes the Guardian of Data (GOD) model, a privacy-preserving framework for evaluating and improving personal AI assistants on-device. The core problem it addresses is the tension between personalization and privacy: proactive assistants need sensitive user data to anticipate needs, but collecting and using such data raises concerns about trust, autonomy, and unauthorized disclosure.

The proposed approach runs inside a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) and generates curriculum-based evaluation tasks that range from simple factual retrieval to more complex cross-domain and proactive recommendation problems. It also introduces data connectors for secure verification, a scoring function based on coverage, quality, and freshness, and anti-gaming safeguards such as identity checks, cross-verification, and fraud penalties.

The paper is not an empirical study with human participants; it is a systems/framework paper focused on on-device personal AI rather than K-12 education. Its main conclusion is that a secure, curriculum-based, privacy-preserving evaluation and training loop can help personal assistants become more proactive while keeping raw user data on device and reducing the risks of fraud, misuse, and loss of trust.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a preprint / framework proposal with conceptual architecture, equations, and illustrative examples, not a peer-reviewed empirical study. It does not report a credible experimental design, comparator, or validated K-12 outcome evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: No K-12 learning or student outcome impact is demonstrated. The paper is about privacy-preserving evaluation of personal AI assistants, with no empirical effect sizes on educational populations or science inquiry outcomes.

interventions.use_case: A privacy-preserving on-device personal AI assistant that uses a TEE-based 'AI school' framework to evaluate and improve proactive recommendations from private user data (email, calendar, receipts, social media) using curriculum-based queries, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning.

Trusted Execution Environment (TEE)-based secure evaluation and grading infrastructure for on-device AI, including data connectors, anti-gaming safeguards, and privacy-preserving verification of user data.
